Canada doesn't have the same system as the USA so there is less voter fraud. In municipal and federal elections, you only vote for one member of parliament. Paper ballots are counted manually by your neighbours in the same room where you voted. Two people are paid to count. The incumbent party in your district has the right to provide one of the counters, the runner up party in that district in the last election can provide the other. (usually the counters are just anybody who filled the call for a day's work). Other parties can have an unpaid volunteer looking over their shoulders. Voter ID laws are in place, but they are not strict enough.

We have a multi-party system, so nobody ever gets a majority of the popular vote. In the last election, the Liberals got 40%, the Conservatives got 32%, the leftist NDP got 19%, the Separatists got 5%, and the Greens 4%. That equated to a Liberal landslide.
